rules.title: Reprisal for reporting violations or tenant union activity prohibited
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not threaten or take reprisals against a residential tenant for enforcing housing laws, reporting suspected housing-code or related violations, exercising specified utility rights, or organizing or joining a tenants’ union. A termination notice, rent increase, or substantial change in tenancy terms within six months after protected activity is presumed retaliatory, except a termination notice for nonpayment of rent.
rules.key_value: 6-month rebuttable presumption; damages of 1 to 3 months' rent or actual damages, whichever is greater

coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies when a residential tenant engaged in protected enforcement, reporting, utility-rights, or tenant-union activity.
coverage.summary: Covers tenants of residential premises in Massachusetts who engage in specified protected housing-related activity.

rules.exemptions: The statutory presumption for a notice of termination of tenancy excludes termination for nonpayment of rent.
rules.penalty: Landlord or agent is liable for damages of not less than one month's rent and not more than three months' rent, or actual damages sustained by the tenant, whichever is greater, plus costs of suit including a reasonable attorney's fee.
rules.interaction: The protected activity includes enforcing or reporting violations of federal, state, or local laws, regulations, by-laws, or ordinances regulating residential premises.
rules.quoted_span: The receipt of any notice of termination of tenancy, except for nonpayment of rent, or, of increase in rent, or, of any substantial alteration in the terms of tenancy within six months after the tenant has commenced, proceeded with, or obtained relief in such action
